entries.proposition: DESIGN: nested case-control within a Chinese occupational cohort: 500 incident T2D cases and 500 age- and sex-matched controls, serum metabolomics on baseline samples, genotypes on the same 1000 people.
entries.snippet: Healthy subjects (n = 500) matched 1:1 by age and sex at baseline were selected as the control group

entries.proposition: The WWOX-linked finding: a SNP in the WWOX region associates with the leucine/isoleucine level, at p 2.92e-6, effect 0.411, minor allele frequency 0.03.
entries.snippet: allele G of rs72487966 is related to an increased leucine/isoleucine level

entries.proposition: Table S3 labels the SNP by NEAREST gene WWOX (chr16:78,432,786, A/G, MAF 0.03, beta 0.411 +/- 0.088, p 2.92e-6): a locus annotation, not a functional link to WWOX. About 60 minor-allele carriers are expected in 1000 people.
Same row, effect columns: minor allele frequency 0.03, beta 0.411 with standard error 0.088, p 2.92e-6.
entries.anchor: Table S3, rs72487966 row, effect columns

entries.proposition: Figure 2E: the leucine/isoleucine Manhattan plot has no point above the red genome-wide line; the WWOX label sits at a point between the blue (suggestive) and red lines. Figure 2F: the regional plot shows a lone peak at about 78.43 Mb (p 2.92e-6) in a wide WWOX intronic region with few supporting SNPs in LD.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2, Manhattan plots (A, C, E) and regional plots (B, D, F) for FFA 20:4 (FADS1, p 2.30e-10), pipecolinic acid (CHRM3, p 5.40e-7) and leucine/isoleucine (WWOX, p 2.92e-6), with suggestive blue and significant red lines.

experimental_context.system: serum metabolome GWAS, 1000 Chinese adults, nested T2D case-control

entries.proposition: The authors themselves grade the WWOX correlation as suggestive and in need of validation.
entries.snippet: However, the correlations were suggestive, and more validation studies are needed.

entries.proposition: The MR result is printed as OR 0.004 with a 95 percent interval of 1.001 to 1.006, a point estimate outside its own interval (an apparent typographical error for 1.004, not corrected by the authors); the MR tests leucine/isoleucine against T2D, with summary statistics from other cohorts, and does not test WWOX.
entries.snippet: the relationship between leucine/isoleucine and T2D was proven to be causal (OR = 0.004, 95% CI 1.001–1.006, p = 0.001)

entries.proposition: The statement that WWOX is a risk gene for T2D is supported only by a citation to the 2012 East Asian meta-analysis index SNP, which is a different variant (rs17797882).
entries.snippet: which is a risk gene for T2D.[ 10 ]

entries.proposition: The Discussion cites the 2019 Han Chinese replication (PMID 31145772) for the statement that WWOX is related to HOMA-beta; that paper reports the association in controls only, at nominal p 0.014 without correction, and no association with T2D. The claim is a restatement of a weak datum.
entries.snippet: The WWOX gene is related to HOMA‐β

entries.proposition: Internal inconsistency: the same adjusted OR, interval and p (0.731, 0.597 to 0.896, p 0.002) is printed for carnitine C14:0 (said to rise and to be positively associated with T2D) and for pipecolinic acid (said to fall); an OR below 1 contradicts the stated direction for C14:0.

Figure 1B plots leucine/isoleucine with an adjusted OR per SD above 1 and two asterisks; the metabolite panel (CMB) adds only a small AUC gain to clinical markers (0.755 to 0.773 discovery, 0.772 to 0.797 validation, Figure 1E and 1F).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1, (A) bubble plot of 81 significant metabolites, (B) forest plot of ORs per SD unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted by class, (C) pathway analysis, (D) forest of CMB, CCB and combination, (E) ROC discovery (CMB 0.708, CCB 0.755, combination 0.773), (F) ROC validation (CMB 0.687, CCB 0.772, combination 0.797).

experimental_context.system: serum untargeted metabolomics, incident T2D vs matched controls

entries.proposition: Population limits stated: Chinese retirees from one city, mean age 63; replication in other centres and ethnic groups required.
